audit.whatIsWrong: The page's single most-repeated claim is wrong twice over. It calls Rebuttal 'her R' in four places (spikes[3].text, early, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0]) — Rebuttal is her W and her R is Golden Eclipse — and it says that engaging into it makes 'your engage damage reflect' back onto you. Rebuttal reflects enemy PROJECTILES; nothing in Maokai's kit is flagged as a projectile.
audit.why: Riot W text: 'a barrier around herself that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage, and grants her movement speed.' Against Maokai the reflect clause is inert — what actually happens is that your damage is blanked and she walks out of the root on the move speed. The mirror (mel__maokai) reached the same conclusion and corrected its own side; this page still tells the reader to fear a reflect that cannot occur, on a 38/35/33/29/26s cooldown they should instead be baiting.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal named as her W with its real effect and 26-38s cooldown in spikes[3].text, early, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], report[5].t and tradeGood.
sources: ownerKit flags — no projectile on any Maokai ability

audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows contradicted their own whys in both layers. Row 0 read Mel though whys[0] says you both have one ability; row 1 read Skill though whys[1] says your combo comes online against a dashless Mel; row 4 read Mel though whys[4] says your R into W lockdown leaves her 'no way out'; row 6 read Maokai though whys[6] says your damage flattens and she executes from range.
audit.why: Mel has no dash and no escape anywhere in her kit, so every stage where Maokai has his root combo is his. Late is the only stage that turns, and it turns to even, not to her.
audit.corrected: Row 0 -> Skill 5/10, row 1 -> Maokai 7/10, row 4 -> Maokai 7/10, row 6 -> Skill 5/10. Matched full+content pairs in one atomic group, matching packet.levelChart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every stage was framed as a 'Solar Snare cooldown window' with no numbers, and the first-item row credited Heartsteel while the content layer credits a Bami/sustain line.
audit.why: Solar Snare is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s at 1000 range; Radiant Volley is 10-6s at 950; Rebuttal is 38-26s. The long cooldown worth waiting on is Rebuttal, not Solar Snare — that is the one that decides whether your all-in connects.

notes:
The reflect error was the worst single claim in my slice. Four strings told the reader that engaging Mel while her barrier is up turns their own combo against them; Rebuttal reflects projectiles and Maokai has none. A player following that advice never presses W into a dashless champion who has no other answer — it inverts the matchup. All four are corrected, plus the slot name (Rebuttal is W, Golden Eclipse is R).

I did NOT assert that Rebuttal's damage-immunity blocks the ROOT itself. Riot's text says it 'prevents her from taking damage' — that is damage, not crowd control, and whether Twisted Advance's root still applies through it is exactly the kind of thing the kit files cannot answer. The page now says it blanks your damage and speeds her out, which is true either way. Flagged in unverified.

The packet defect 'never names any of Mel's abilities' is now largely closed: Rebuttal, Solar Snare, Radiant Volley, Golden Eclipse and Overwhelm all appear. Searing Brilliance is still unnamed.

The mirror's Sap Magic finding applies here too and is worth stating from this side: Radiant Volley deals damage repeatedly inside its area, and Sap Magic's cooldown drops each time Maokai is struck by a spell, so her signature poke is the fastest way to refill your own heal. Every string with band room was already carrying a more urgent correction, so it did not land on the page this pass — it is the best remaining upgrade here.

Champion-level kit-flag defect (ninth and last time in this slice): Maokai's Q carries a 'grounding' flag Riot's description does not support. Not asserted anywhere in my twelve matchups.
